- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.20) and price is trending up, model may overestimate momentum — reduce forecast slope by 10–15%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in forecast vs true, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window — apply a 2–3% downward bias to first 7–10 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast with 3-day moving average or apply 10% dampening factor to volatility spikes.
